clue.text: With pleasure about, to bed!

indicators.note: about means the word for pleasure is placed around the next piece

parts.note: pleasure, enjoyment, is fun
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone heads off to bed gladly, as if bedtime were a treat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts FUN around TO, giving FU-TO-N.
explanation.definitionFit: A futon is a Japanese-style mattress used as a bed, often on a low frame.

clue.text: Be suitable to finish off some taxidermy?

definitions.meaning: to attach the beak to a stuffed bird, completing it

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to be just right for a need, and literally a bird's beak would complete a stuffed specimen.

clue.text: Associate of Phi Beta Kappa, say, cheers University

definitions.text: Associate of Phi Beta Kappa, say

parts.note: ta and cheers are both informal British thanks

explanation.surface: A member of an American honour society toasts the university.
explanation.walkthrough: Phi Beta Kappa looks like the US honour society, but these are three Greek letters; the answer is another of them.
explanation.definitionFit: Tau is a letter of the Greek alphabet, keeping company with phi, beta and kappa.

clue.text: Kiss and cuddle endlessly with sailor — sweet stuff

indicators.note: endlessly means the last letter of the word for kiss and cuddle is dropped

parts.note: to neck is to kiss and cuddle
a tar is a sailor

explanation.surface: A sailor's endless smooching is described as sweet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' drops the last letter from NECK, leaving NEC.
explanation.definitionFit: Nectar is the sweet liquid in flowers, and any delicious drink.

clue.text: Persuasive material is to follow, about beers

indicators.note: about means the word for following goes around the beers

parts.note: to stalk someone is to follow them stealthily
ales are beers

explanation.surface: Advertising copy promises more to come, all about beer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps STALK around ALES: S-ALES-TALK. 'is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A sales talk is the persuasive patter used to sell goods, so it is persuasive material.

clue.text: Sure to stop eating stewed dates for starters

indicators.note: stewed fruit is cooked down, so these letters are reworked

parts.note: to fast is to stop eating

explanation.surface: A dieter is determined to give up food, having stewed dates as a first course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stewed' rearranges DATES into STEAD, which comes first ('for starters') before FAST. 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Steadfast means firm and unwavering, which is sure in the sense of steady and reliable.

clue.text: Slowly advanced, nothing more

parts.note: to advance money is to lend it, so advanced means lent
O is nothing, zero

explanation.surface: A loan was gradually made, and that was all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'more' is a link saying the O is added on.
explanation.definitionFit: Lento is the musical direction for a slow tempo.

clue.text: College year remains in disarray at first

indicators.note: in disarray means the letters are thrown into a muddle
at first takes the opening letter of year

explanation.surface: A college's annual leftovers lie in a mess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at first' gives Y from year; 'in disarray' shuffles Y with REMAINS.
explanation.definitionFit: A seminary is a college for training priests or ministers.

clue.text: Continental area unfortunately seized by European country

indicators.note: seized by means the next word is held inside the country's name

parts.note: Austria is a European country
alas is an exclamation meaning unfortunately

explanation.surface: A whole region is sadly annexed by a European state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seized by' puts ALAS inside AUSTRIA: AUSTR-ALAS-IA.
explanation.definitionFit: Australasia is the region comprising Australia, New Zealand and nearby islands, a continental area.

clue.text: Extent of knowledge about Russia's foremost composer

indicators.note: about means the word for knowledge goes around the letter

parts.note: ken is one's range of knowledge

indicators.note: foremost picks the opening letter of Russia's

explanation.surface: Someone with knowledge of the leading Russian composer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts R, the first letter picked by 'foremost', inside KEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Jerome Kern was an American composer of musicals such as Show Boat.

clue.text: Staff with little time to manage church given ages

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time
to run a business is to manage it
an eon is an age, a vast stretch of time

explanation.surface: A clergyman's staff manages a church for ages with little spare time.
explanation.definitionFit: A truncheon is a short club or baton, a kind of staff carried by police.

clue.text: Chap offering no opening for treats?

definitions.text: Chap offering no opening for treats?

indicators.note: no here means the following letter is removed from the word for chap

parts.note: a chap is a mister, a man

indicators.note: opening for means the first letter of the word treats

explanation.surface: A man who never lets anyone in for a treat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no' removes T, the first letter picked by 'opening for' treats, from MISTER. Read whole, the clue also describes someone who never stands anyone a treat.
explanation.definitionFit: A tight-fisted person hoards money and never pays for treats for others, which is exactly a stingy hoarder.

clue.text: Terminology from golf and soccer in obscure places?

parts.note: a hole is a term from golf, the target on each green
taken as written
a corner is a term from soccer, a kick taken from the corner flag

explanation.surface: Sports jargon from two games turning up in unexpected places.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is a British idiom meaning secretive or furtive, done out of sight.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes things done secretly, tucked away out of sight in obscure corners.

clue.text: Tragic figure in the badly-repaired coat

indicators.note: in means the coat sits inside the rearranged letters
repaired means the letters are fixed into a new order

parts.note: a mac is a raincoat

explanation.surface: A character in a tragedy wears a poorly mended coat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repaired' turns THE BADLY into LADYBETH; 'in' puts MAC inside.
explanation.definitionFit: She is the ambitious, doomed wife in Shakespeare's tragedy set in Scotland.

clue.text: Behaviour left blokes in debt, short of billions

indicators.note: in means the next pieces are placed inside the shortened word
short of means the letter for billions is taken away

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship
men are blokes

explanation.surface: Bad conduct left some men owing money, though not billions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short of' takes B from DEBT, leaving DET; 'in' puts PORT and MEN inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Deportment is the way a person carries themselves, their bearing and conduct.

clue.text: Germ linked to English seaside resort

parts.note: a germ in the botanical sense is a bud, the start of growth

explanation.surface: Bacteria are blamed on a seaside town in England.
explanation.walkthrough: BUDE is a seaside resort in Cornwall, south-west England. 'linked to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cornish town is a coastal holiday destination popular with surfers and families.

clue.text: Song with liquid associations, pub song, left half-finished

parts.note: a bar is a pub
a carol is a song

indicators.note: half-finished means only the first half of the word left is kept

explanation.surface: A drinking song from the pub is left incomplete.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-finished' keeps LE, the first half of LEFT.
explanation.definitionFit: A Venetian gondolier's song is a boating song, hence its watery associations.

clue.text: A line in handbag material?

definitions.meaning: a line of schoolchildren walking in pairs
the reptile leather used to make luxury handbags

explanation.definitionFit: Crocodile is British slang for a file of walking children, and also the skin used for bags.

clue.text: Attorney with support getting off first assailant

parts.note: Att is the abbreviation for attorney

indicators.note: getting off first means the opening letter is removed

parts.note: a backer is a supporter

explanation.surface: A lawyer with a supporter gets off first in court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting off first' drops B from BACKER, leaving ACKER.
explanation.definitionFit: An attacker is someone who assaults another, an assailant.

clue.text: Left to copy? It shows lack of talent

parts.note: a copy is an imitation

explanation.surface: Being left only to copy others reveals a want of ability.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It shows' is a link pointing to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A limitation is a shortcoming or weakness, such as a lack of ability in something.

clue.text: No limits to industrial action in European city

indicators.note: no limits means the outer letters of the word for industrial action are cut off

parts.note: a go-slow is a form of industrial action where workers deliberately slow down

explanation.surface: Workers stage an unrestricted protest in a continental capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No limits to' strips G and W, the first and last letters, from GOSLOW.
explanation.definitionFit: The capital of Norway is a city in Europe.

clue.text: Storyline in most of the book?

indicators.note: most of means the last letter is cut away

parts.note: a book is a read, as in a good read

explanation.surface: The plot runs through most of a novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' trims THE to TH. 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A thread is the line of a story or argument that runs through it.

clue.text: New view of earth?

parts.note: the word earth is what results when the letters of heart are rearranged

explanation.surface: A fresh perspective on our planet.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as wordplay: a rearrangement of HEART makes EARTH, which is what the clue's 'of earth' points to.
explanation.definitionFit: A change of mind or attitude is a new view of something.

clue.text: Leave the spot — it's no use waiting for him!

definitions.text: it's no use waiting for him!

parts.note: to go is to leave
a dot is a spot

explanation.surface: Someone told to clear off from a place is not worth waiting for.
explanation.walkthrough: In Beckett's play Waiting for Godot, the title character never arrives.
explanation.definitionFit: The figure in the Beckett play is awaited endlessly but never turns up, so waiting is futile.

clue.text: Some observe Saul is a Biblical character

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Watching King Saul, someone notes he is a figure from the Bible.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'is' into the definition; it is a link, and the definition is 'a Biblical character'.
explanation.definitionFit: Esau, Jacob's twin brother in Genesis, is a figure from the Old Testament.

clue.text: Meat, pale by the sound of it

indicators.note: by the sound of it signals that a word is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: a pale is a fence post, a stake

explanation.surface: Some meat looks rather pallid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pale' looks like an adjective but is the noun for a pointed fence post.
explanation.definitionFit: A thick slice of beef cut for grilling or frying is a common meat.

clue.text: Return and impress

definitions.meaning: to go back to your house by car
to make a point forcefully so that it sinks in

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both travelling back to your house by car and forcefully making a point understood.

clue.text: Spinning brother's globe

indicators.note: spinning means the word is turned round, read backwards

parts.note: bro is short for brother; that the clue word itself begins with these letters is a coincidence

explanation.surface: A brother's globe is set turning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spinning' reverses BRO.
explanation.definitionFit: An orb is a sphere or globe.

clue.text: Beaming woman who'll get you in a row?

definitions.text: Beaming woman who'll get you in a row?

parts.words: Beaming woman who'll get you in a row?
parts.note: a cinema attendant shines a torch beam to guide you to your seat in a row, not someone smiling or arguing

explanation.surface: A smiling woman who will land you in a quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beaming' suggests smiling and 'row' an argument; really it is a torch beam and a row of seats.
explanation.definitionFit: Theatre and cinema attendants used torches to show patrons to their seats in a row.

clue.text: Underground had briefly held back opening

indicators.note: held back means the pieces are read from back to front

parts.note: the Tube is the London Underground
'd is the short form of had

explanation.surface: A train on the Underground was briefly held up at its start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'held back' turns TUBE plus D into DEBUT.
explanation.definitionFit: A debut is a first appearance, the opening of a career or show.
